fixes.explanation: That's the reason the LORD gives. He says, “…because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as his possession.” So none of that land is going to Israel, “…not even a footprint…” Not one footprint's worth! When God hands something to somebody, friend, it's theirs, and that's the end of it.

Yes! The note says the descendants of Esau drove out the Horites and settled in their place, “…just as Israel did in the land that the LORD gave them as their possession.” So the note lines up Esau's people in Seir with Israel in their own land. I love a little side note that quietly says, 'You're not the only ones, baker.'

Twelve is a long stretch already, friend. But the road from Kadesh-barnea to the Brook of Zered was longer than that. It took thirty-eight years, and it ended when that whole generation of fighting men had perished from the camp (Deuteronomy 2:14). Twelve falls way short of that.

Seven years would be a long trip, I'll give you that. But the text gives a much bigger number for the road from Kadesh-barnea to the Brook of Zered, thirty-eight years (Deuteronomy 2:14). Seven doesn't even get you halfway, friend.

True! When they get close to the Ammonites, the LORD says, “…do not harass them or provoke them…” And He gives His reason: “…for I will not give you any of the land of the Ammonites.” Notice the pattern, friend. That's Edom, then Moab, and now Ammon, and each time the LORD says the land is already given.
